# LOWN: Look Only When Needed

> LOWN (Look Only When Needed) is a training-free decoding method for diffusion vision-language models (DVLMs). It predicts the masked tokens without the image and processes the image only when this prediction disagrees with the last image-conditioned prediction. Paper: "Look Only When Needed: Certificate-Guided Visual Routing for Efficient Diffusion VLMs" (arXiv:2610.36671).

Authors: Donghyeon Cho (KAIST)*, Joowon Kim (KAIST)*, Seungho Shin (KAIST), Eunho Yang (KAIST, AITRICS)†. *Equal contribution, †Corresponding author.

From the abstract:

- Visual tokens make up 89-97% of LLaDA-V's input on the benchmarks studied, so most of the decoding computation is spent repeatedly processing the same image.
- Removing the image changes a token being unmasked at only 22.8% of decoding steps on average and at as few as 7.9%.
- Agreement certifies the earlier prediction for reuse, and the number of certified tokens sets how many are unmasked in that step.
- Without training or a tuned threshold, LOWN retains 99.6% of LLaDA-V's score on ten benchmarks at 35.3% of the decoding FLOPs on average.
- LOWN also generalizes across LLaDA-based DVLMs, composes orthogonally with visual token pruning, and runs under key-value caching for further efficiency gains.

Citation:

```bibtex
@article{cho2026lown,
```
